thread:
Lia: Heads-up — hitting a weird async kernel / symbol mismatch when running AWQ quantized nova-9b on TRT-LLM across L40s nodes. Nodes become 'unhealthy' after warmup and requests fall back.
Samir: can you paste the short log snippet?
Lia: sure, pasted below:
```
[trtllm] WARN kernel_fallback: expected kernel id=0x2, got 0x1, falling back
E trtllm_plugin: unresolved symbol: trtllm_plugin_init_v3
E runtime: async kernel queue failed: code=702 (kernel mismatch)
``` 
Lia: stack shows plugin load failure immediately after KV cache warmup (~50 steps).
Chen: two quick checks — driver vs container CUDA mismatch, and RDMA / nv_peer_mem. Are you on the OFED nodes?
Lia: yes, these are the RDMA-connected L40s instances in prod pool. Image is redwood/trtllm:cuda18-prod built last week.
Maya: we've seen a similar noise before where RDMA exposing GPU memory changed the expected cuCtx lifetime and trt plugins failed to find the right symbol. Error there was slightly different but same outcome: plugin init fails.
Infra-bot: rolling update started for pool 'l40s-quant-prod' at 2026-03-20T12:02:00Z (3 -> 6 nodes)
Samir: can you run `ldd /opt/trtllm/lib/libtrtllm.so` and paste the top unresolved entries? Also `nvidia-smi -q | grep 'Driver Version' -A2` and `modinfo nv_peer_mem`.
Lia: attaching quick outputs:
```
$ ldd /opt/trtllm/lib/libtrtllm.so
	libcuda.so.1 => not found
	libnvrtc.so.11.5 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvrtc.so.11.5
	libcudnn.so.8 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudnn.so.8
$ nvidia-smi | head -n5
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Driver Version: 535.86.10  CUDA Version: 12.3                                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
$ modinfo nv_peer_mem
	filename: /lib/modules/5.15.0-xx-generic/kernel/drivers/infiniband/rdma_cm/nv_peer_mem.ko
	version: 1.1
```
Lia: note libcuda not found inside container — we bind-mount /usr/lib from host normally so not sure why it's missing only in failing nodes.
Chen: that points to host/container ABI mismatch — container expects libcuda in a different path or a different SONAME. If libcuda isn't resolvable, plugin symbols won't link -> undefined symbol at dlopen time.
Maya: also check GLIBC: if host glibc != container glibc, ldd can show 'not found' too. But the RDMA angle is real: when nv_peer_mem is present, some allocs expose different handles and TRT-LLM's plugin expects to call `cuCtxGetCurrent` which might be null under certain RDMA setups.
Samir: quick mitigation: set env TRT_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTODETECT=1 and TRT_FORCE_SOFT_FALLBACK=1 to force trtllm into a safer path; throughput will drop but it should avoid crash.
Lia: tried that — with TRT_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTODETECT=1 the runtime falls back to vLLM driver and requests succeed (throughput down ~4x) so app stays up. Good safety net.
Chen: long term fix options:
- rebuild trt-plugins against host libcuda/driver (match 535.xx);
- ensure container binds the host's libcuda.so.1 into /usr/lib or update rpath; 
- test with TRT-LLM v0.10.1 plugin which added a guard for null cuCtx in plugin_init (we are on v0.9.4 currently).
- add an RDMA smoke test in CI that toggles nv_peer_mem and runs AWQ quant smoke.
Samir: I'll spin a single L40s repro without RDMA first. If repro only with nv_peer_mem on, that's our smoking gun.
Lia: creating a minimal repro job now on a single node (disabling autoscaler). Will run the AWQ quant pipeline and attach profiler + TRT_KERNEL_DEBUG logs.
Deploy-bot: Created ticket #INC-4129: "trtllm: async kernel mismatch on AWQ quant path with RDMA present" assigned to eng-ml.
Maya: small extra note — when you run with `TRT_KERNEL_DEBUG=1` you might see messages like "kernel meta version mismatch: expected v2, recorded v1" which means the kernel registry inside the plugin was built against a different header set.
Lia: confirmed TRT_KERNEL_DEBUG showed exactly that. Putting full logs into the ticket. Running step1 (single-node repro) now, will update in ~30m :thumbsup:
Samir: if you want a dedicated L40s to speed up repro, ping infra and I'll carve one from the Reserved pool.
Lia: thanks — will ping if the single node repro is flaky.
